name: VirtualList
description: A list too long to render whole — a mailbox, a contact book, a log. Only the items near the screen are in the DOM; the rest is space.

props.name: items
props.description: Every item, however many — only the ones near the screen are rendered.

props.name: itemKey
props.description: Who an item is: stable across renders, since an item's measured height is kept under it.

props.name: children
props.description: Draws one item: a `List.Item`, a `SwipeItem` — one `<li>` per item, and nothing around it.

props.name: estimateSize
props.description: What an item counts as until one has been drawn, in px — then the mean of those drawn. Default 57, a `md` item.

props.name: overscan
props.description: Items kept either side of what is on screen, so a fast scroll has something to show. Default 6.

props.name: initialCount
props.description: How many items render before anything is measured — on a server, and in the first frame. Default 20.

props.name: onRangeChange
props.description: Fires when the rendered range moves. The way to fetch more: load the next page when `endIndex` nears the end.

props.name: scrollerRef
props.description: What scrolls the list, when it is not the nearest scrolling ancestor — or, with none, the page.

props.name: tag
props.description: `ol` when the order means something — steps, a ranking. Default `ul`.

a11y: Each rendered item carries `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset`, so a screen reader says "12 of 4,000" rather than counting the twenty in the DOM.

The item focus is in stays rendered while the list scrolls away from it, so Tab carries on from where it was; and since Tab scrolls its target into view, the window follows the keyboard down the list.
Find-in-page cannot see an item that is not rendered. A list that has to be searchable that way is one to render whole — or to give a search field of its own.
